portInfo.description: Juneau’s cruise operation concentrates on the downtown Gastineau Channel waterfront. The City and Borough of Juneau Docks & Harbors page states two city cruise docks downtown and two private docks in the area, together serving over one million passengers each May–September season. City docks are described as berthing one Panamax ship up to 1,000 feet and one post-Panamax ship up to 1,100 feet, with berths completed in 2017 and later seawalk/bus-staging uplands work. Public amenities listed include a pedestrian promenade, visitor center, bus staging, public parking, and a Port/Customs building with a Port of Juneau Field Office and U.S. Customs and Border Protection offices. Exact berth names, private-dock operators, and passenger-door coordinates are **Not verified** on the page captured — pins stay null.

thingsToDo.shortCall: **≥4 h.** Downtown promenade + one nearby attraction; skip glacier if tender/queue risk exists. ≥90 min buffer.
thingsToDo.standardCall: **≥6 h.** Mendenhall or tram **or** whale tour — pick one major outing; ≥90–120 min return.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Combine glacier + downtown only with overnight or a very late all-aboard; Juneau has no road connection to the rest of Alaska’s highway system for “drive onward” improvisation.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Identify whether you are on a **city** or **private** dock before assuming a two-minute walk to the same storefront block — CBJ itself distinguishes the two dock categories.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: CBJ downtown cruise berths — Two city docks; ≤1,000 ft / ≤1,100 ft framing
gettingThere.publicTransport: **From the docks.** CBJ lists promenade, visitor center and bus staging on the waterfront. Timed walks to specific downtown blocks **Not verified**. **Airport (JNU).** Transfer minutes from cruise docks **Not verified** on the harbors page. **Tenders.** Page describes dock berthing, not a primary tender operation — still confirm sailing documents if weather forces anchorage.
